title: GEO vs SEO: which should you invest in for 2026?
meta_description: Both, in a ratio set by where your buyers ask. How to split the budget, what each one moves, and the four cases where the answer is clearly one or the other.
h1: GEO vs SEO: which should I invest in for 2026?
extract_html: Keep the SEO you have and put new money into GEO in proportion to how many of your buyers now ask an AI engine before they search. The two overlap less than people assume: only about 12 percent of the URLs ChatGPT cites rank in Google's top 10 for the same question, while Google's own AI Overviews still take about 38 percent of their citations from the top 10. So SEO keeps you in Google's AI answers and GEO gets you into ChatGPT's, and for most B2B and considered-purchase brands the budget ends up split rather than switched.
body_html:
Start with where the answer is formed

SEO earns you a position on a results page; the buyer still clicks and reads. GEO earns you a mention inside an answer the buyer may never click through from. Those are different outcomes, and in 2026 they are decided by different pages.

  • Google's AI Overviews draw about 38 percent of their citations from the top 10 organic results[1]. If you rank, you have a head start in Google's AI answers.
  • ChatGPT and Perplexity read a different web: only about 12 percent of the URLs they cite rank in Google's top 10 for the original prompt[2]. Ranking well helps little there; being discussed on the pages they retrieve helps a lot.
  • Across engines, the most-cited domains are communities, reference sites and review platforms rather than brand sites[3], which is why GEO is mostly work on other people's pages.

What each one moves, in 2026 numbers

SEO and GEO compared on what they produce and what they cost to keep
SEOGEO
The outcomeA click from a results pageA mention or recommendation inside an AI answer, with or without a click
Where the work happensMostly your own site, plus linksMostly the pages engines already cite: lists, directories, Reddit threads, publishers; your own pages second
What is happening to itClicks from informational queries are falling where AI Overviews appear: organic click-through on page one fell by roughly a third over 2025 in a study of 5.47 million queries[4], and a 300,000-keyword comparison found the top result losing 58 percent of its clicks[5]Growing with usage, but inconsistent run to run: the same prompt names different brands within an hour[6], so it is measured as a share over many runs
Time to see movementMonths for new rankingsDays for owned-page fixes, 6 to 10 weeks for earned placements
How long it lastsAs long as you hold the rankingAs long as the cited page stays cited; the lists and threads engines favour are often a year or more old

Four cases where the answer is clear

  1. Your buyers ask AI first and your brand is absent. B2B software, agencies, professional services, considered consumer purchases. Run ten of their questions on ChatGPT; if competitors are named and you are not, GEO is the gap and SEO will not close it.
  2. You rank well and sell on Google. Local services, transactional ecommerce, anything where the buyer still clicks through to compare and buy. Keep the SEO budget; most of your Google AI Overview presence rides on it anyway[1]. Add GEO for the questions that start the journey, not the ones that end it.
  3. Your traffic is informational and falling. If your best pages answer how-to questions and the clicks are leaving because the answer now appears above the results[7], more SEO on those pages buys less every quarter. Shift the content budget towards pages that get cited and towards being named when the engine recommends.
  4. You have no SEO base at all. Fix the basics first: crawlable pages, a clear answer in the first paragraph, schema. They serve both. Then decide the split from the ten-question test above.

How to split the budget

Take your buyers' top 20 questions and run each on ChatGPT, Gemini and Google. Score each question: does an AI answer form before any click, and are you in it? The share of questions where the answer forms first and you are missing is roughly the share of new spend that should go to GEO. For most of the B2B brands we audit that lands between a third and a half; for a transactional ecommerce brand ranking well it can be a tenth. Whatever the split, keep one set of frozen prompts and track both numbers monthly, because the ratio will move as your buyers do.

What not to do

  • Do not cut SEO to fund GEO on Google. Google's AI answers are built partly from the ranking you would be giving up.
  • Do not buy GEO as "more content". The pages that decide AI answers in most categories belong to someone else; new blog posts on your own site are a small share of citations.
  • Do not judge either on one screenshot. A share over hundreds of runs is the only number that survives the inconsistency[6].

How Redaccel approaches it

We do GEO, not SEO, and we say so. The free AI visibility audit runs your buyers' questions on the engines, shows per engine whether you are named and who is, and lists the pages that decide it. If the audit shows Google's AI answers already carry you and ChatGPT's do not, that is the split, and the audit says so before you spend anything. The longer explainer is on GEO vs SEO.

faq.q: GEO vs SEO: which should I invest in for 2026?
faq.a: Keep your SEO and add GEO in proportion to how many of your buyers ask an AI engine before they search. SEO carries you into Google's AI Overviews, which take about 38 percent of citations from the top 10; GEO gets you into ChatGPT and Perplexity, where only about 12 percent of cited URLs rank in Google's top 10. Most considered-purchase brands end up splitting rather than switching.

No, but clicks from informational queries are falling where AI answers appear, by roughly a third on page one in one 5.47-million-query study and by 58 percent for the top result in another. Transactional and local searches still convert through clicks, so SEO keeps earning there.

faq.q: Does good SEO automatically give me AI visibility?
faq.a: On Google, partly: AI Overviews lean on the top 10. On ChatGPT and Perplexity, mostly not: they cite communities, lists and review sites that rank nowhere for the query. Being named there is separate work.

faq.q: How do I decide the split for my brand?
faq.a: Run your buyers' top 20 questions on ChatGPT, Gemini and Google. The share of questions where an AI answer forms before any click and you are not in it is roughly the share of new spend that belongs to GEO.

sources: Ahrefs (Louise Linehan), "Update: 38% of AI Overview Citations Pull From The Top 10", March 2026. 863,000 keyword SERPs, 4 million AI Overview URLs.
Ahrefs, "Only 12% of AI Cited URLs Rank in Google's Top 10 for the Original Prompt", 2025.
Semrush, "The Most-Cited Domains in AI: A 3-Month Study"; corroborated by Statista, 2026.
Seer Interactive, "AIO Impact on Google CTR: 2026 Update", Tracy McDonald, Hannah Cooley and Marketa Williams, 24 April 2026. 53 brands, 5.47M tracked queries, January 2025 to February 2026.
Ahrefs, "Update: AI Overviews Reduce Clicks by 58%", Ryan Law with Xibeijia Guan, 4 February 2026. 300,000 keywords, December 2023 vs December 2025.
SparkToro (Rand Fishkin, with Gumshoe.ai), "New Research: AIs are highly inconsistent when recommending brands or products", January 2026. 600 volunteers, 12 prompts, 2,961 runs.
Pew Research Center, "Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears in the results", 22 July 2025.
